name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__discover_services
description: Find things the user can buy, book, order, or pay a service for — across the Coinbase Bazaar (EVM-heavy) and pay.sh (Solana-heavy) x402 catalogs; e.g. physical goods on Amazon/Shopify, gift cards and mobile top-ups, flights and travel, market and crypto data, SMS, document parsing, contact enrichment, and other paid APIs. Reach for this whenever a request means buying, ordering, booking, or using a paid service and no dedicated PayBox tool already covers it — the user does NOT need to say "x402" or "crypto". It only searches and reads live 402s and moves no money (paying is a later `use_service`/`pay_x402` step the user still gates). The default result is a curated set; `query` searches it, while `raw=true` is only for debugging the uncurated catalogs. pay.sh entries carry a catalog-derived price hint and the call method in the description; the live 402 is the source of truth. Some routes come from the provider's API spec and have no price hint (empty `accepts`) and a templated URL like `/air/intents/{intent_id}/book` — substitute the real path values and read the live 402 for the price; these are how multi-step flows are completed. When such a route needs a JSON body, the description carries its shape as `· body {field*:type,...}` (`*` = required) — send exactly those fields via `use_service`. If health filtering empties the result, that means no curated service currently has fresh passing health—not that the catalogs are empty. Without the health gate, follow `suggested_next_call` before concluding there are no services. name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__get_request
description: Keep checking one request with the same `request_id` until it reaches `success`, `denied`, or `error`. Use this for `pending_approval`, `pending_signature`, `pending_confirmation` (broadcast and waiting on-chain), or `pending_settlement` (bridge in flight); confirmation and settlement polls refresh the authoritative state. Never re-call the original operation to finish the same request. The exception is an expiry: a terminal `error` or `denied` with `retryable: true` means it timed out before signing and nothing was spent, so re-issue the original request once. Only the client that created the request can read it.

request_id.description:
Request UUID returned by a prior request_payment / request_wallet_sign /
request_secret call (in the `request_id` field).

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__list_credentials
description: Start here. Lists the wallet, card, and secret credentials this connector can use, with `credential_id`, kind, approval mode, and safe metadata such as wallet address/chains or card brand/last4. It also returns `ungranted`: active credentials the user owns but has not granted this connector, each with `credential_id`, `name`, `kind`, and safe metadata (wallet chain family, card brand/last4). To gain access, pass those `credential_id`s to `request_account_change`'s `add`. Use a returned granted ID for operation tools; use `get_portfolio` for live balances.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__list_requests
description: Read-only history of this connector's own requests, newest first. Filter by status and paginate with `limit`, passing both `before` and `before_id` from the last row for the next page. Pending rows can be stale and outputs are redacted, so call `get_request` with a request's ID for its current state or actual artifact.

before.description:
Keyset cursor for the next page (first half): the `created_at` of the last
row from the previous page, as RFC3339. Must be paired with `before_id`.

before_id.description:
Keyset cursor for the next page (second half): the `request_id` of the last
row from the previous page. Paired with `before`; the two together form a
total cursor, so requests sharing a `created_at` are never skipped.

limit.description: Max rows to return, newest first. Defaults to 200, capped at 500.

status.description:
Optional status filter (snake_case): `pending_approval`,
`pending_signature`, `pending_settlement`, `pending_confirmation`,
`success`, `denied`, or `error`. Omit to list every status.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__moonx_resolve_binding
description: Signing-app only. Resolves and caches the MoonX `key_id` and `derivation_path` when a parked signing operation is missing its wallet binding. The private agent key stays in the app and the MoonX secret stays server-side. Agents should not call this tool.

agent_signature.description:
Hex of the Ed25519 signature over `signed_body`, made with the agent's
private key inside the iframe.

api_pub.description: The agent's Ed25519 public key (lowercase hex, no 0x) — `api_pub`.

request_id.description: The `request_id` of the parked wallet sign this binding is for.

signed_body.description: Hex of the UTF-8 JSON `{issued_at}` the iframe built and ed25519-signed.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__moonx_sign
description: Signing-app only. Performs the MoonX signing step for a parked PayBox signing operation using an app-signed envelope. The private agent key stays in the app and the MoonX secret stays server-side. Agents should use the initiating operation and poll `get_request`, not call this tool.

agent_signature.description:
Hex of the Ed25519 signature over `signed_body`, made with the agent's
private key inside the iframe.

api_pub.description: The agent's Ed25519 public key (lowercase hex, no 0x) — `api_pub`.

request_id.description: The `request_id` of the parked wallet sign this signature is for.

signed_body.description:
Hex of the UTF-8 JSON envelope the iframe built and ed25519-signed
(`{raw_signing_payload,key_id,derivation_path,issued_at}`).

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__pay_x402
description: Create an x402 payment proof from a granted wallet; this tool does not fetch the paid content. Pass the 402's `accepts` exactly; for v2 also pass `x402_version=2` and its `resource` block from `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, while v1 needs neither. For a delegated wallet with auto-undelegate, PayBox returns one composite undelegate_then_x402 request, so do not assume a terminal error means no on-chain step happened. Follow `pending_signature` or `pending_approval`, then poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` to terminal; never re-call this tool for that request. On success, use `output.value.x_payment` to retry the original resource. When telling the user what this charged, quote `plan.x402.amount_usd` (already formatted in dollars) — do not convert the atomic `accepts`/`accepted` amount or `amount_cents` yourself.

credential_id.description: Wallet credential UUID to pay from (from `list_credentials`).

resource.description:
The 402's `resource` block — v2 only, from the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header.
Echoed verbatim in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` payload; omit for v1.

x402_version.description:
The 402's `x402Version` (1 or 2), which picks the proof header: 1 →
`X-PAYMENT`, 2 → `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Read it from the 402 you received: 1
if `accepts` came in the JSON body, 2 if it came in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`
response header. Defaults to 1.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_account_change
description: Open the PayBox account window to change this connector's credential access. Pass `add` (ungranted `credential_id`s from `list_credentials.ungranted` to grant), `remove` (granted `credential_id`s to revoke), `create` (brand-new credentials to make then grant, each `{kind, chain?, name?}` — use only when nothing suitable exists in `ungranted`), and/or `set_mode` (change a granted credential's approval mode, each `{credential_id, mode}` where mode is `always_approve` or `autonomous`). `note` is an optional one-line reason shown to the user. The returned `manage_url` changes nothing by itself: the user confirms in their own session (their passkey). A newly granted or created wallet is NOT usable until the user pastes its fresh signing key back into the PayBox window — `list_credentials` will show it granted before that, so do not treat that as signing access. Wait for the user to confirm or for the blocked operation to succeed on retry before saying access changed.

create.description:
Brand-new credentials to create then grant — use only when nothing
suitable exists in `list_credentials.ungranted`.

note.description:
Optional one short sentence describing why access is changing — shown to
the user in the paybox window as context. E.g. "needs an EVM wallet to
sign".

remove.description: Granted `credential_id`s to revoke from this connector.

set_mode.description:
Change the approval mode of already-granted credentials — e.g. switch a
card from "always_approve" to "autonomous" (full access) or back.

CreateCredentialRequest.description:
A brand-new credential the connector asks the user to create then grant.
Only descriptors — the user makes it in their own session.

chain.description:
For wallets, the chain to create on (e.g. "ethereum", "base",
"solana"). Ignored for cards and secrets.

name.description: Optional display name for the new credential.

SetModeRequest.description: Ask the user to change one granted credential's approval mode.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_payment
description: Authorize a merchant-scoped, one-time virtual card for a card purchase. This does not submit checkout, charge the merchant, or top up an account. If it returns `pending_approval`, share the `approval_url` and poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` to a terminal state; never re-call `request_payment` for that request. On success, call `claim_payment_credentials` once if the card is redacted, use it at the merchant, and only say paid after the merchant confirms.

amount_cents.description: Amount in minor units, using the currency supplied below.

credential_id.description:
Credential UUID, returned by `list_credentials`. Must point to a
card-kind credential.

merchant.description:
Merchant identifier the agent is paying — opaque to paybox; surfaced
in the audit log and shown to the user during approval.

merchant_url.description:
Real HTTPS origin or merchant URL that Basis Theory binds the one-time
card to. Do not synthesize this from the merchant name.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_secret
description: Request a granted secret. `raw=false` returns a one-time `secret_token`; `raw=true` returns the actual secret, and `purpose` explains the request to the user. If it returns `pending_approval`, share the `approval_url` and poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` to terminal; never re-call `request_secret` for that request.

credential_id.description:
Credential UUID, returned by `list_credentials`. Must point to a
secret-kind credential.

purpose.description:
Short description of why the secret is being requested. Shown to
the user during approval, recorded in the audit log.

raw.description:
When true, paybox returns the raw secret value (e.g. an API key).
When false (default), paybox returns a one-time-use secret token
that the caller can exchange via a downstream resolver — useful
when you want to avoid the raw value transiting an LLM.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_swap
description: Quote a token swap from a granted wallet using an intent, not a built transaction; `amount` is in the source token's smallest units. The PayBox signing app signs client-side and the server broadcasts; an unsupported route fails before anything is parked. `pending_signature` is autonomous, while `pending_approval` needs the user's passkey. Poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` through `pending_confirmation` for same-chain swaps or `pending_settlement` for cross-chain swaps to terminal; never re-call this tool for a `pending_approval`, signed, confirming, settling, or terminal request — that executes a second swap. Stuck-window recovery only: if it stays autonomous `pending_signature` for at least 30 seconds of polling and the user reports the signing window is closed or missing, poll once more immediately, then re-issue the exact operation at most once to re-open it. Across VMs, pass a destination-chain `recipient` unless PayBox can resolve the user's single vaulted wallet there.

amount.description:
Amount in `src_token`'s smallest unit, as a decimal string (mirrors
MoonX `getAction`).

dst_chain.description:
Destination chain key. Omit for a same-chain swap (defaults to
`src_chain`); a different chain bridges, settling asynchronously
(`pending_settlement` until the bridge delivers).

dst_token.description:
Destination token address, or exactly "native" for SOL when the
destination chain is Solana.

recipient.description:
Optional recipient address on `dst_chain`; defaults to the wallet's own
address — except across VMs (e.g. Solana → an EVM chain), where it
defaults to the user's single vaulted wallet on the destination VM and
is otherwise required.

slippage_bps.description:
Slippage tolerance in bps (default 150 = 1.5%). Becomes the on-chain
`amountOutMin`, so it is the safety floor for autonomous execution.

src_chain.description:
Source chain key (CAIP-2, e.g. "eip155:8453" for EVM or "solana:mainnet"
for Solana); must be in the credential's `chains`.

src_token.description:
Source token address ("native" or the zero address for the chain's
native asset, e.g. ETH).

value_cents.description: Rough USD value of the sell side, for policy thresholds.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_transfer
description: Send native SOL/ETH or a token to a recipient from a granted wallet — this moves real funds. Pass `chain`, `to` (recipient), and `amount` in the token's smallest units (wei/lamports/base units); omit `token` for the native asset, or pass the ERC-20 contract (EVM) or SPL mint (Solana). PayBox builds and broadcasts the transaction; the wallet signs client-side. `pending_signature` is autonomous, while `pending_approval` needs the user's passkey. Poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` through `pending_confirmation` to terminal; never re-call this tool for a `pending_approval`, signed, confirming, settling, or terminal request — that sends a second transfer. Stuck-window recovery only: if it stays autonomous `pending_signature` for at least 30 seconds of polling and the user reports the signing window is closed or missing, poll once more immediately, then re-issue the exact operation at most once to re-open it.

amount.description:
Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string (wei for native
ETH, lamports for native SOL, or the token's base units).

chain.description:
Chain key (CAIP-2, e.g. "eip155:8453" for EVM or "solana:mainnet" for
Solana). Must match the wallet's VM (an EVM wallet sends on any EVM
chain; a Solana wallet on solana:mainnet).

to.description: Recipient address on `chain` (EVM `0x...` or Solana base58).

token.description:
Token to send: omit for the chain's native asset (ETH/SOL), or pass the
ERC-20 contract (EVM) / SPL mint (Solana) address.

value_cents.description: Rough USD value of the send, for policy thresholds.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__request_wallet_sign
description: Sign with a granted wallet in the in-chat PayBox window. Prefer a structured intent—message, EIP-712 data, EVM transaction or authorization, or Solana message or transaction; `raw` remains a supported escape hatch for a precomputed digest. PayBox never holds the key and returns the signed artifact without broadcasting a wallet-sign transaction. `pending_signature` can sign now; `pending_approval` needs the user's passkey first. Poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` through every pending state to `success`, `denied`, or `error`; never re-call this tool once it is signed or if it is `pending_approval`. The exception: while it is still autonomous `pending_signature` and the user has not signed, re-issuing the identical request re-opens the signing window and reuses the same parked request (no duplicate).

credential_id.description:
Credential UUID, returned by `list_credentials`. Must point to a
wallet-kind credential.

intent.description:
What to sign — see `WalletSignIntent`. This is the *only* description of
the operation: paybox decodes it for approval; sanctions checks only the
stored wallet address. The window signs client-side (paybox never sees the
key). Accepts the object OR a JSON string of it (see
`deserialize_intent`). The chain, destination, and value are read from
the intent — there are no separate declared fields.

WalletSignIntent.description:
Intent to sign. You pass *what* to sign, not a pre-hashed digest —
paybox's signing app builds the correct bytes (EIP-191/712, RLP tx,
EIP-7702, Solana message) and assembles a broadcast-ready artifact. Pick
the `op` matching the wallet's chain. `raw` is an escape hatch for a
pre-computed digest on a chain the others don't model.

oneOf.description: EIP-712 typed data (the full typed-data object) → 65-byte signature.

EVM transaction (eip1559 fields; bigints as decimal strings) →
serialized tx ready for `eth_sendRawTransaction`.
Arbitrary Solana message; `address` is the base58 wallet pubkey.
Solana tx (base64 of the serialized unsigned tx) → signed base64 tx.
Escape hatch: sign a pre-computed digest (hex) as-is.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__submit_envelopes
description: Signing-app only. Completes a parked swap, x402 payment—including composite undelegation—or plugin money request from ordered app-signed envelopes checked against the server-held plan. PayBox broadcasts transactions or assembles the payment proof, and the call is idempotent. Agents should invoke the original operation and poll `get_request`, not call this tool.

envelopes.description:
One agent-signed signing envelope per parked tx, IN ORDER (an `approve`,
when present, before the `swap`). Each is `{api_pub, signed_body,
agent_signature}` — the iframe sends NO transaction bytes; the server
already holds the txs it quoted and signs+encodes+broadcasts them.

envelopes_json.description:
Same payload as `envelopes`, encoded as JSON. The MCP Apps host can
normalize arrays of app-provided objects in some clients; the signing
iframe uses this field so batch cardinality survives the app boundary.

SignEnvelope.description:
One agent-signed signing envelope, posted by the signing iframe in the
server-completes model — the SAME shape as the `moonx_sign` tool, one per
parked transaction (in plan order). The iframe holds the agent keypair and
builds + ed25519-signs `signed_body`; it sends NO transaction bytes (the
server already holds them, pinned at park time), so it cannot substitute a
different transaction.

agent_signature.description: Hex of the Ed25519 signature over `signed_body` (agent private key).

api_pub.description: The agent's Ed25519 public key (lowercase hex, no 0x) — `api_pub`.

signed_body.description:
Hex of the UTF-8 JSON envelope the iframe ed25519-signed:
`{raw_signing_payload, key_id, derivation_path, issued_at}`. Its
`raw_signing_payload` MUST equal the EIP-1559 sighash of the parked tx at
the same index — the server re-derives and checks this before spending
the MoonX secret key on `/sign`.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__submit_signature
description: Signing-app only. Submit the signed artifact for a parked wallet-sign request, bound to its original `request_id`; swaps, x402, and plugin operations complete through `submit_envelopes` instead. Agents should poll `get_request`, not call this tool.

artifact.description:
The signed artifact produced client-side by the signing window — the
op-specific object: `{"signature":"0x..."}`, `{"serializedTransaction":
"0x..."}`, `{"authorization":{...}}`, or `{"signedTransactionBase64":"..."}`.

request_id.description:
The `request_id` of the parked wallet sign (from the
`request_wallet_sign` result / the `pending_signature` payload).

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__use_service
description: Fetch an x402 resource and let PayBox handle the payment and paid re-fetch. Follow the target service's API documentation or the OpenAPI-derived route description returned by `discover_services` for the exact URL, method, headers, and JSON body; PayBox handles payment but does not infer the target API contract. A delegated wallet may produce one composite undelegate_then_x402 request, so do not assume a terminal error means no on-chain step happened. `mode="probe"` makes one unpaid diagnostic request (sending any `body` you pass, so a POST endpoint returns its real 402 rather than a 411), creates no payment request, and does not prove paid success. For a pending paid call, poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` to terminal and never re-call this tool to finish that request. At terminal `success` or `error`, inspect both `output.value.payment` and `output.value.resource`; `output.value.response` remains for compatibility. If `resource.ok=false`, inspect `payment.status` before saying whether payment succeeded, was rejected, or is unknown; do not report full success or retry blindly, because another call may require another payment. When telling the user what this charged, quote `plan.x402.amount_usd` (already formatted in dollars) — do not convert the atomic `accepts`/`accepted` amount or `amount_cents` yourself. Popular x402 services include `brij` (book flights), `purch` (buy on Amazon), `agentmail` (an email inbox), and `glim.sh` (read live X/Reddit/web/YouTube data); discover more with `discover_services`.

body.description: Optional JSON request body (for POST/PUT services).

credential_id.description: Wallet credential UUID to pay from (from `list_credentials`).

headers.description:
Optional custom request headers (name → value), forwarded on both the 402
probe and the paid call — e.g. an x402 service's required `x-agent-id`.

method.description: HTTP method for the call (default GET).

mode.description:
Optional mode. Omit or set "pay" to pay an x402 endpoint. Set "probe"
to make one unpaid diagnostic request: no payment, typed data, signing
iframe, request row, or payment artifacts.

url.description: The paid x402 resource URL to fetch.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__verify_solana_balance
description: Prove that one confirmed Solana transaction changed an exact wallet and SPL or Token-2022 mint, then return the current raw token balance from an Alchemy read at or after that transaction's slot. Pass the canonical wallet address, token mint, and transaction signature. This is read-only and moves no funds. `read_covers_transaction=true` proves the returned Alchemy read includes that transaction; it does not mean MoonX or `get_portfolio` has indexed it.

address.description: Canonical base58 Solana wallet address whose token balance changed.

token_mint.description: Canonical base58 SPL or Token-2022 mint affected by the transaction.

transaction_signature.description: Canonical base58 64-byte Solana transaction signature to verify.

input_schema.description: Shared input contract for the MCP and REST transport adapters.
input_schema.title: VerifySolanaBalanceArgs

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_buy_outcome
description: Buy a YES or NO World position from a granted Solana wallet. Pass the outcome mint and an exact-in `size` in atomic USDC units, not a built transaction; PayBox pins the buyer and sender from the credential. If the signing window reports a region block, tell the user to turn off their VPN if they have one, then click "Check again" in the same window; never create a second request for that trade. Approval follows the grant: autonomous returns `pending_signature`, while approval-gated returns `pending_approval`. Poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` through `pending_confirmation` to terminal; never re-call this tool for that request.

credential_id.description:
Wallet credential UUID (Solana wallet-kind), from `list_credentials`. The
buyer + on-chain sender are pinned from THIS credential, never the agent.

market_mint.description:
The outcome (YES/NO) SPL mint to buy — from `world_get_market` /
`world_orderbook`.

size.description:
Amount to spend in the SMALLEST UNITS of USDC (atomic integer string; e.g.
1000000 = 1 USDC). A buy is exact-in USDC.

slippage_bps.description:
Slippage tolerance in bps (default 150 = 1.5%). The safety floor for the
order price.

value_cents.description: Rough USD value of the trade, for policy thresholds / display.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_change_position
description: Add to or reduce a World position from a granted Solana wallet. Use `side="buy"` with `size` in atomic USDC units, or `side="sell"` with `size` in atomic outcome-token units; PayBox pins the owner and sender from the credential. If the signing window reports a region block, tell the user to turn off their VPN if they have one, then click "Check again" in the same window; never create a second request for that trade. Approval follows the grant: autonomous returns `pending_signature`, while approval-gated returns `pending_approval`. Poll `get_request` with the same `request_id` through `pending_confirmation` to terminal; never re-call this tool for that request.

market_mint.description: The outcome (YES/NO) SPL mint of the position to change.

side.description: "buy" to add to the position or "sell" to reduce it.

size.description:
Amount in SMALLEST UNITS (atomic integer string). For side "buy" it is the
USDC to spend (e.g. 1000000 = 1 USDC); for side "sell" it is the
outcome-token to sell.

value_cents.description: Rough USD value of the trade, for policy thresholds / display.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_filter_outcome_mints
description: Map up to 200 SPL outcome-mint addresses to the World markets whose exact YES or NO mint matches. This is read-only and useful for identifying World tokens found in a wallet.

addresses.description:
Outcome mint addresses to look up (max 200). Returns the markets whose
YES or NO mint matches one of these.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_find_markets
description: Browse World markets or grouped events without moving funds. Filter by status, event, or series and page with `cursor`. Results are ordered by volume only within each fetched page, so do not treat the first page as globally ranked or complete. Use the returned tickers and outcome mints for market details or a trade.

cursor.description:
Optional pagination offset (World's `cursor`): the number of rows to
skip. Pass the `cursor` from a prior response to page forward. Applies
to both the events and markets lists.

event_ticker.description:
Optional event ticker to filter the markets list to one event (ignored
for the events list). Validated server-side.

events.description:
List events (each groups its markets) instead of the flat markets list.
Defaults to false (markets).

limit.description: Optional cap on how many rows to return (World's `limit`).

series_ticker.description:
Optional series ticker to filter the EVENTS list to one series (World's
`seriesTicker`; ignored for the markets list). Distinct from
`event_ticker`. Validated server-side.

status.description:
Optional status filter (World's `status`): one of active | initialized |
determined | finalized. Applies to both lists. Validated server-side.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_get_market
description: Get one World event by its event ticker, with its nested markets by default. Returns each market's ticker, status, and YES/NO outcome mints without moving funds. Get the event ticker from `world_find_markets`.

event_ticker.description:
The World EVENT ticker to fetch. Returns the event and, with
`with_nested_markets`, its markets.

with_nested_markets.description: Include the event's nested markets in the response. Defaults to true.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_market_prices
description: Get a World market's YES/NO quote history by ticker between Unix-second `start_ts` and `end_ts`, with an optional supported sampling resolution. This is read-only and useful for showing how the market moved.

resolution.description:
Optional sample window in seconds (1, 5, 15, 60, 300, 900, or 3600;
World defaults to 60).

ticker.description: The World market ticker to read price history for.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_orderbook
description: Get the best YES/NO bids and asks, sizes, slot, and timestamp for a World market. Pass a market ticker, or an outcome mint with `by_mint=true`. This is read-only; a null side means there is no live quote, such as after determination or finalization.

by_mint.description:
Treat `id` as an outcome mint address instead of a market ticker.
Defaults to false (ticker).

id.description: A World market ticker, or (with `by_mint=true`) a YES/NO outcome mint.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_positions
description: List a Solana wallet's World prediction-market positions, classified. Read-only: no funds move, nothing is signed, no credential is touched. Its `items` and `total_usd` use the same outcome pricing as get_portfolio. `items` is the raw live balance feed, not the final position classification. For a previously known outcome mint missing from `items`, check `positions`, `settled`, `position_result`, and `coverage` before explaining it; `position_result` in either list is the official classification. If neither list contains it, or `coverage.history_available=false` / `coverage.trades_truncated=true` / `coverage.market_data_available=false` leaves the answer unresolved, use `world_filter_outcome_mints` with that exact mint. For this exact-mint fallback, only report won or lost when finalized `status`, `result`, and the mint's exact YES/NO side prove it; otherwise say unknown. Never infer sold, no balance, won, lost, or not-yet-indexed from absence alone. A WON position settles into CASH (the outcome token is burned at settlement), so a winner holds CASH rather than the outcome token; cash out by swapping CASH to USDC via `settlement_cash.cash_out` (request_swap). `settlement_cash` is top-level and separate from any position. `coverage` flags unavailable market/history data or truncated history. Use before world_change_position or world_redeem.

address.description:
Solana wallet address to read World positions for. Returns classified
`positions`/`settled` entries (each with a `position_result`) plus a
top-level `settlement_cash` for a settled winner's CASH cash-out. Public
on-chain data.

name: mcp__claude_ai_PayBox__world_redeem
description: Redeem a settled World outcome position from a granted Solana wallet. First call `world_positions`, then pass candidate `items[].tokenAddress` values to `world_filter_outcome_mints` and use the exact matched outcome mint; raw balances do not classify winners or guarantee a payout. Pass `size` in atomic outcome-token units. PayBox quotes that outcome token to USDC; when World has no route, it reports nothing to redeem. If the signing window reports a region block, tell the user to turn off their VPN if they have one, then click "Check again" in the same window; never create a second request for that trade.
